current.text: He is expected to start at center for Charlotte on opening night.
Charlotte's center plan is not settled. Diabaté, the rookie taken 14th and Ryan Kalkbrenner compete for the job. Steinbach is also in the mix, and Grant Williams plays some small-ball five.
The added competition at center is a threat to his role and caps his upside. One expert does not see him as a long-term starting solution.
In a late-season stretch last season he played about 28 minutes a game, and Charlotte had the top offensive rating and the fifth-best defensive rating. He won Hustle Player of the Year.
Worth a late flyer outside the top 100, around round 10 or 11. He slid past round 12 in one mock draft but usually goes earlier.
One expert would draft him over Ryan Kalkbrenner about 90 times out of 100 because he is expected to start, even though Kalkbrenner may produce more at equal minutes.
One expert is not confident that he keeps up his shot blocking.
Charlotte plays 4-3-4 games in our playoff weeks 19 to 21 and has only 13 back-to-backs, the league minimum.
Charlotte's system stresses steals and offensive rebounds, which fits his game.

durable.text: He is an undersized center who works as a hustle player and one of the best offensive rebounders in the league.
He is a good defender who switches onto ball handlers, but he cannot really protect the rim, so his blocks are modest for a center.
He is improving as a passer on short rolls.
He makes no threes. His value comes from FG% on low volume and rebounds, and he gives few points.

note: Yahoo ranks him 145 and ESPN 160, and both price him at 0 to 1 USD, so in a 144-player draft he is a 1 USD endgame center or a waiver add. Experts call him a round 10 to 11 flyer because he should start, and he helps with FG% and rebounds. He gives no threes, few points and a weak FT% on low volume. In the first weeks, check that he keeps the starting job and about 25 minutes ahead of the rookie and Kalkbrenner. If he loses the job, drop him.
